content.title: Layout Investigation: Find the Broken Relationship
content.hook: Good layout debugging is not “try CSS until it looks okay.”
content.context:
You are looking for the rule that controls the relationship you care about.

Use this loop:

**describe the intended relationship → inspect the parent → inspect the relevant layout property → make the smallest change → verify the changed case**
goals: Investigate a layout defect by identifying the intended relationship, observing the active rule, and making the smallest justified change.

options.text: Whether `flex-direction` is creating the vertical arrangement.
Whether the button text is spelled correctly.
Whether the page needs a new HTML document.
Whether the screen is too bright.

feedback.correct: The symptom is directly connected to the direction rule. Start with the rule that controls the relationship instead of changing unrelated properties.
feedback.incorrect: The symptom is directly connected to the direction rule. Start with the rule that controls the relationship instead of changing unrelated properties.

options.text: `align-items`
`color`
`border-radius`
`font-size`

feedback.correct: The problem is cross-axis placement. `align-items` is the property that expresses that relationship for the flex container.
feedback.incorrect: The problem is cross-axis placement. `align-items` is the property that expresses that relationship for the flex container.

content.question:
A three-column grid looks fine wide and cramped narrow.

You see no responsive rule.

What is the smallest useful question?

options.text: At what available width does this relationship stop working, and should the grid change there?
How can I add 40 random margins?
How can I hide the cards?
How can I delete half the content?

feedback.correct: The symptom is about the relationship between the grid and the available width. Find the constraint boundary before changing unrelated styles.
feedback.incorrect: The symptom is about the relationship between the grid and the available width. Find the constraint boundary before changing unrelated styles.

options.text: `flex-wrap: wrap`
`color: red`
`border: none`
`font-weight: bold`

feedback.correct: The intended relationship includes another row when space runs out. `flex-wrap: wrap` expresses that directly.
feedback.incorrect: The intended relationship includes another row when space runs out. `flex-wrap: wrap` expresses that directly.

content.title: Smallest-fix challenge
content.text:
Imagine a card grid switches to one column too early.

Your first instinct is to add more rules.

Stop.

Ask:

1. What width causes the current relationship to stop working?
2. Which rule controls that change?
3. What is the smallest edit that proves or disproves your hypothesis?

That sequence is more reliable than changing five values at once.

content.question: Which investigation order is most reliable?

options.text: Intended relationship → controlling rule → smallest change → verify.
Random changes → refresh → random changes.
Rewrite the whole page → inspect later.
Change every spacing value first.

feedback.correct: Good layout investigation starts with a model of the intended relationship and changes only the rule you have reason to suspect.
feedback.incorrect: Good layout investigation starts with a model of the intended relationship and changes only the rule you have reason to suspect.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Layout bugs are relationship bugs.
**Senior habit:** Make the smallest change that tests your hypothesis.
**Mastery signal:** You can identify the controlling layout property from a visible symptom before editing anything.
